NoteTexAccessor::text_only¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteTexAccessor::text_only() const

Project Each Cell Onto Its Prose, Dropping Math¶

text_only() removes every complete math region from a Text cell — recognizing $...$, $$...$$, \(...\), and \[...\] the same way math_only does — and keeps everything else, collapsing the resulting whitespace gaps to one ASCII space and trimming the cell. It is the exact prose-preserving mirror of math_only, which keeps the formulae and drops the prose; the two together partition a cell’s visible content into its two halves.

This method is a shape-preserving projection, not a ragged extractor. One input cell always produces one output cell. A cell that is entirely math becomes the empty string, which preserves its location in a matrix or higher-rank Note. An unmatched opener — a $ with no closing $ before the cell ends — is not treated as a region boundary, so the unmatched dollar and the text after it are kept as ordinary prose.

Delimiter recognition is shared with the math extractors: an escaped dollar (\$) is literal prose, not an opener; $$ is recognized before a plain $; and a single-dollar region cannot cross a physical newline. Content outside any math region — including any TeX commands there — is retained exactly, byte for byte aside from whitespace collapsing; text_only() does not itself strip commands or comments.

The receiver is not mutated. A new Text Note with the same rank and shape is allocated, including for scalar and empty-shaped inputs. Undefined input stays undefined, and every defined non-Text dtype is rejected before transformation.

Example 1: All Four Delimiter Forms And An Unmatched Opener¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(Before $x^2$ after)", R"(A \(y+1\) B \[z\] C)",
    R"(price \$5 and $unfinished)", ""});
std::cout << source.tex().text_only() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["Before after", "A B C", "price \\ unfinished", ""]

The first two cells lose their math and keep the surrounding prose, with the gap it left collapsed to one space. In the third cell, \$5 is literal prose (\ survives — see the note below), and the unmatched $unfinished is never closed, so it is never treated as math and its text is kept as-is. The empty cell stays empty.

\$ unescapes to a bare \ here because text_only() copies retained prose byte for byte without re-escaping; only the $ that made the pair a literal dollar sign is consumed by the delimiter scanner, leaving the backslash behind exactly as read.

Example 2: Idempotent On Already-Prose-Only Input¶

const auto prose_only = source.tex().text_only();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << (prose_only.tex().text_only() == prose_only).all().bool_item()
          << '\n';

Output¶

true

Once every math region is gone, a second call has nothing left to remove.

Example 3: A 2-D Grid, Shape Preserved¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{"left $x$", "$y$ right", "plain", "$$z$$"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << grid.tex().text_only() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["left", "right"], 
  ["plain", ""]
]

The fully-math last cell reduces to the empty string in place, keeping the grid’s shape intact.

Example 4: Undefined And Non-Text Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().text_only().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().text_only();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "text only Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
text only Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • math_only: the exact prose-dropping mirror of this method.

  • math_blocks: keep every math region as a separate ragged token instead of discarding it.

  • to_text: a broader prose extraction that also strips commands and comments, not just math regions.
